style: Read clearly and naturally, at a moderate pace
lines: Welcome to Outbreak Model. Pick a story, press Play, and watch the count grow.
Notice the milestones. Each time the count gets ten times bigger, it takes the same amount of time.
Try the log scale. An exponential curve turns into a straight line.
Ask when. Drag the target line to any number, and logarithms will tell you exactly when the count gets there.
Want to test your instinct first? Turn on Guess first, drop a pin on the time axis, then show the answer.
Three bases, one answer. Base two, base ten and base e all give the same time, because they describe the same curve.
Press Check it to run the clock to that exact moment.
Hit the ceiling. A real outbreak runs out of people, so the pure exponential stops telling the truth.
This is a made-up example to explore the math. It is not a forecast of any real illness.
